 Most recent Most popular 'A good PR man' published at 22:24 GMT 22:24 GMT 
 FT: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland 
 Pat Nevin 
Former Scotland winger on BBC Sportsound 
 If I'm ever in trouble and I need a PR man, I'm getting him because he's absolutely good at it. 
 He's certainly a glass-half-full person. You can talk away any moment and say it's just a moment, but it's four moments, five moments, six moments. He speaks so incredibly well, but that doesn't really change anything. We've been beaten again.
 A really horrible thing in that situation is that if I am running the SFA, I'd be asking the players what they think and just saying tell us the truth, what do you think? Are you backing us? 
 If a couple of the main ones say we're not sure, we're not sure of the decision-making, then you know. I think it's got to that stage.

 'This camp is good for future' - Pocognoli published at 22:21 GMT 22:21 GMT 
 FT: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland 
 More from Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli: "I think if we were in confidence, we would not produce the moments we produce in the game. 
 "I think we create good moments on the ball, on pure bravery decisions to play forward through the lines or the pressure. 
 "We create chances also for pressing, sometimes we should have to manage better the transition from pressing, but it is all the things we want to see.
 "So the next step is to have the quality to just finish this action, and the more we have games together, the more we will try to fix these things. 
 "We have a lot of good response from this camp and it's good for the future as well."

 'Score doesn't reflect game' - Pocognoli published at 22:17 GMT 22:17 GMT 
 FT: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland 
 Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli tells BBC Scotland: "The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game, if I'm really
honest and objective. 
 "I think we had some very good moments in the game, we started the game
like we wanted, aggressive away from home. 
 "We could decide to be low on the pitch, but we did what we wanted to plan. 
 "I think we
played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments in the game, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes
and adapted well from the first minute. 
 "I think we conceded the goal from maybe one of the
first chances they had. 
 "We also created chances, maybe even closer to the goal, but
we missed it, it means we were not clinical in that moment in the box. 
 "In the second half, yeah, we started
poorly from the first minute, a poor corner we gave away. 
 "Then you feel that, OK, we will
get punished.
 "But I think when we made the substitutions, the substitutions made an impact, and we should have
scored two goals in that period. 
 "We got punished for the same reason like in the first half. 
 "At the end, it's a bad feeling, the score, but I think that the players try to do their best and create
moments that we want to see."

 Well, Iain, Scotland would have to go some way to fail to qualify for a tournament they are co-hosting.
 Along with fellow co-hosts England, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, they will have to qualify through their group, but two places will be reserved at the finals should any of the host nations fail to qualify.
 The qualifying draw takes place in Belfast on 6 December, with group fixtures starting in March next year.

 Time is up for Pocognoli, obvious his 3-4-3 system doesn't work and he refuses to change it to suit games. All through this group of games he has played that system with players out of position. I can't see us qualifying for the Euros on home soil if the SFA stick by him for the start of the qualifiers.

 'The manager has to get time, but he has to win games' published at 22:02 GMT 22:02 GMT 
 FT: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland 
 Scott Brown 
Former Scotland captain on BBC Scotland 
 Image source, Reuters I'm with Tom 100%. As soon as Steve Clarke left I was in the same boat, saying he's that guy that's brought us to two Euros and a World Cup, nobody had done that since 1998. 
 The manager has to get time, but he has to win games. We have to be harder to beat and that's what Clarke did. He knew our limitations. 
 This fast-flowing, open football isn't going to work overnight. It's going to take a lot of time and you need the players to do it. 
 107 112 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Pocognoli system's a dud' published at 21:59 GMT 21:59 GMT 
 FT: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland 
 Tom English 
BBC Scotland's chief sports writer on BBC Sportsound 
 I thought that performance was amateur hour. When the SFA appointed Pocognoli, Craig Mulholland started talking a lot about data and metrics. The data I see is they've conceded seven goals in two games against Switzerland. They've conceded four against Switzerland's B team playing in third gear. 
 This is on the players as well, who are not as good as some people seem to think. The manager certainly has to carry the can for this, I know he's only in the door, but these players look disjointed, they're easy to play through. 
 His system's a dud. I don't think he's going to be in this job much longer. 
 The players have to take some of the blame, but this is also on the manager, his coaches, Mulholland, the person who in great fanfare unveiled Pocognoli and said loads of clubs were after him. 
 This is where Scotland are, they've regressed. 
 I know Steve Clarke was in the job a long time, but Scotland lost 3-0 against Brazil and people thought that was a poor result, they're now losing 4-0 to a weakened Switzerland team. This is going backwards at a fair rate of speed.

 'We don't have time, we've got to step up' - Robertson published at 21:53 GMT 21:53 GMT 
 FT: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland 
 Scotland captain Andy Robertson tells BBC Scotland: "First half, I thought we were in the game, we lost a stupid goal, but I thought we had chances and it could have been 2-1 at half-time.
 "By the time you get to 50 minutes and you're 3-0 down, that can't happen in international football.
 "We were playing a good team, but I felt we were in the game, it is a really tough night for us.
 "I dont think you've got time in international football, you have to do it. These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden, who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.
 "We don't have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up.
 "We have a long break now to March, which is not a good thing, and it is going to be a tough one to swallow.
 "We really need to step up again, as in international football, you do not have time."

 At a glance 
 First-half Ferguson own goal sets second-string Swiss side on way
 Quick-fire double from Boteli & Sanches at start of second half
 Amdouni's late deflected strike seals comfortable win
 Scots finish third in group, leaving them in pot three for Euro 2028 qualifying
 By Amy Canavan BBC Sport Scotland at Sitterstadion, St Gallen Scotland's uninspiring Nations League campaign ended with a humbling defeat against much-changed yet still superior Switzerland to bring further questions over the work of head coach Sebastien Pocognoli. 
 The Scots required victory in St Gallen - as well as a favour from North Macedonia in taking points off Slovenia - to finish second and secure a pot two seeding in next month's Euro 2028 qualifying campaign.
 Five minutes into the second half at the Sitterstadion and their part in that deal was dead and buried.
 Quick-fire goals from Winsley Boteli and Alvyn Sanches added to Lewis Ferguson's unfortunate - but clumsy - own goal, which undermined Scotland's decent start.
 Robertson eclipses Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped man 
 Published 2 hours ago 
 On a historic night, where captain Andy Robertson became the most-capped men's international on his 103rd appearance, the Scots turned in a slipshod showing.
 They were back to their old tricks, shooting themselves in the foot through Bologna midfielder Ferguson's mistake, before being sliced and diced by the World Cup quarter-finalists' second-string side.
 Boteli's replacement, Zeki Amdouni, added insult to injury late on with a deflected strike, resulting in a damning and potentially damaging result for Pocognoli, who has won two and lost three of his opening six games.
 Two days away from the one-year anniversary of their famous victory against Denmark, where the never-say-die attitude was apparent and belief palpable, such qualities appear a stretch away from this easily beatable Scotland side.
 Scotland analysis: Pocognoli has lots to ponder 
 And so Pocognoli's first act is up already.
 There was a 10-15 minute period in the first half where the Belgian's promised methods - a solid, united, high press - was at the best the Tartan Army have seen.
 A cohesive Scotland team pushed their classy hosts, twice coming close from the heads of Aaron Hickey and John McGinn.
 The latter's attempt was particularly tame, while the former went off injured, again. The early signs suggest another hamstring problem. The Brentford right-back just can't catch a break.
 Perhaps that's how Pocognoli is feeling, too. Questions surrounding him, his system and his methods will surely only drag on over the next four months before his side play again.
 This campaign was understood to be one of learnings, of trial and error. There has been plenty of the latter, but little of the former. Perhaps if Scotland were failing through invention and imagination, there'd be a greater acceptance.
 But with one shot on target - that barely memorable - and a handful of wasted opportunities, it was all too lacklustre.
 Pocognoli's first four games came in quick succession and, while there wasn't too much grace in this two-game camp, he now has lots of time. And lots to ponder.
